title: Operation of a Benchtop Bioreactor
protocol: Calibrate pH probe before installation and sterilize with the vessel.
Install pH probe in the headplate.
Install pO2 probe in the headplate.
Install harvest pipe in the headplate at an adjustable height.
Hook gas sparger up to the gas source on the fermentor and mount it in the headplate.
Mount impeller shaft and install impeller.
Install exhaust gas condenser.
Clean vessel and headplate with soap and water using a soft brush.
If media is not heat labile, add it to the clean vessel until maximum working volume is reached (3.3 L for a 5 L total volume vessel).
Mount vessel headplate ensuring o-ring seal is properly seated.
Install antifoam probe into its 10 mm port.
Install the harvest pipe into its 10 mm port.
Put a piece of tubing on the top of it and clamp it off.
Install tubing and a 0.20 μm filter on the sparge inlet.
Then clamp this off.
Gather 2 reference buffers in small beakers, a wash bottle, and a spare wash beaker.
Hook the pH probe up to the fermentor and turn the fermentor on.
Scroll to the pH parameter and using the menu button, scroll to the 'Cal' option.
Press 'Enter'.
Select '2' for 2 point calibration.
Wash off the probe tip and submerge it in the low reference buffer.
Adjust the displayed value to match the value of the low reference buffer.
Once it stops blinking, press 'Enter'.
Wash the probe off and insert it into the second reference buffer.
Allow the value to stabilize and then use the keypad to make the displayed value match the high reference buffer value.
Press 'Enter' to confirm.
Wash the probe tip off and disconnect it from the fermentor.
Put the protective cap on the connection and install it in the headplate.
Open the pO2 probe tip and check to ensure that there is enough electrolyte to cover the tip.
If not, add some to the reservoir and close it back up.
Install the pO2 probe in the headplate.
Make sure that the autoclave cap is put on to protect its electrical connections.
Obtain a bottle for reagent feed with a dip tube and air filter.
Add pump tubing to the dip tube port and attach the other end to the inlet port on the fermentor.
Place tubing on all unused ports then clamp tubing off.
Install a 0.45 μm filter on the exhaust gas condenser.
Check that all tubes that go below the level of the media are clamped off to prevent media from coming out.
Put the vessel in the autoclave for 25 - 30 min at 121 °C, liquid cycle.
Install the vessel on the fermentor base.
Hook up the pH probe cable.
Attach the pO2 probe cable.
Hook the sparger up to the gas addition rotameter.
Sterilely add 1 M NaOH reagent to the bottle with the dip tube and install the pump head on the base pump head spindle.
Put the temperature sensor in the thermowell on the headplate.
Ensure that it goes all of the way to the bottom of the thermowell.
Lower the agitation arm onto the vessel's impeller coupling.
Make sure that the fermentor is on.
Check that water is available to the fermentor.
Turn on the air supply to the fermentor.
Scroll to the temperature parameter and set the temperature to 37 °C.
Press the 'Enter' button to start the temperature control.
Turn the gas flow to 1 vessel volume of media per minute or less.
For this setup, gas flow is 3 L/min.
Set agitation parameter to 300 rpm.
Press 'Enter' to turn on agitation.
Scroll to pH parameter and set it to 6.8 once temperature reaches 37 °C.
Turn pH control on by pressing 'Enter'.
Set agitation speed to maximum of 1,000 rpm for the run.
Ensure pO2 probe is properly polarized.
After 2 hours, scroll to pO2 parameter and select 'Calibrate Function' with 1 point calibration using 'Menu' button.
Wait 15 minutes and set pO2 value to 100 by pressing 'Enter'.
Scroll to agitation and turn the 'Cascade' to 'on' in the menu.
Set pO2 value to 30.
Press 'Enter' to start pO2 control.
Start the control software package on the PC.
Calibrate probes, stabilize agitation at 300 rpm, set temperature to 37 °C and pH close to 6.8 before inoculation.
Sterilize the port for inoculation with alcohol.
Draw inoculum into a syringe and add it to the sterilized port.
Close the port.
Mark time of inoculation in log book.
Take a sample at sterilization time.
Sterilize the end of the harvest pipe tube with alcohol.
Open the clamp covering the harvest port.
Use a syringe to draw a sample and discard it.
Use another syringe to pull another sample for analysis.
With a third syringe, push air back through the pipe to remove dead volume from the line.
Clamp the line off after pushing air.
Determine the cell density of the culture.
Record the pH value of the culture.
Log values every hour for microbial cultures as needed.
Sample the culture one final time for endpoint values.
Receive endpoint values for cell density and possible pH or measurement of wet cell weight.
Open the headplate and dispose of the contents in a designated "kill tank".
Add bleach or other antimicrobial agents to the kill tank.
